headline: YOUTUBE NOW SAYS BOOSTING A CREATOR'S VIDEO LIFTS CONVERSIONS 30 PERCENT.  IN MAY IT SAID 20, FOOTNOTED TO THE IDENTICAL TWELVE MONTHS OF DATA, AND NEITHER NUMBER HAS EVER CARRIED A SAMPLE SIZE
deck: The claimed effect went up by half while the data behind it stayed exactly where it was.  The new figure does not appear in the 25-page pack it promotes, only in the post promoting it.  And the one study in the whole document with a published sample measures what people remembered and said they intended, not what anybody bought.
tldr: YouTube's claim for boosting a creator's video moved from 20 percent conversion lift in May to 30 percent in October, footnoted to the identical twelve months of data, with no sample size published for either and the new figure appearing only in a social post rather than in the 25-page pack it promotes.  Ask your Google representative in writing for the sample size, the definition of conversion lift and the reason the same dataset now reads differently, and build your business case on the Kantar study instead — 4,342 people, a disclosed control group, and brand metrics rather than purchases.

Ruggable moved about a million dollars out of its Meta performance budget into creators on ShopMy and reports roughly three million dollars of revenue in month one, doubling then tripling, but the money replaced its worst-performing affiliate networks rather than adding a budget line.  Rank your affiliate networks by incremental revenue this week, put the bottom tier's budget through a creator-commerce platform on a ninety-day test, and leave one weak network running so you can tell a better channel from a better budget decision.

Marketers put measurement at the top of the difficulty list at 67 percent and negotiation and contracting at the top of the recoverable-waste list at 60 percent, on a base of 78 ANA members, with the stated cause being that nobody owns the creator relationship so two business units negotiate separately with the same person.  Sort your last two quarters of creator contracts by creator name to find the ones your company signed twice, and name one owner for creator negotiation across business units before buying another measurement tool.

Almost 60 percent of Twitch's hours watched happen outside its top thousand channels, while 80.4 percent of CHZZK's happen inside them, and about 63 percent of Kick's 19.4 percent annual growth came from its own tail.  Re-split your live budget by channel rank band for each platform rather than by platform name, and ask any live proposal which rank band the promised hours are coming from before you sign it.

A six-hour creator League of Legends tournament peaked at 414,000 and held an average of almost 307,000 across 1.9 million hours watched — a bigger peak than the record grand final of a tier-one Dota 2 series — while the same creator's first edition in May had peaked at 920,800.  Ask for average concurrents and airtime alongside peak on every creator-event proposal, and price a second edition at about half the first one's peak until somebody shows you otherwise.

The 25 largest United States advertisers now spend 5.5 percent of revenue on advertising against 6.1 percent in 2019, with Big Tech sitting 52 billion dollars below its own 2019 intensity, while consumer goods went the other way to 12.5 percent.  Weight your prospecting toward consumer goods this quarter and argue your next internal case in ratio rather than in absolute budget, because the ratio is the number their finance team is managing.

YouTube is piloting an invite-only monthly Shorts bonus that pays for upload consistency and counts organic views only, so advertising money behind a creator's Short contributes nothing to their bonus.  Ask your Shorts talent whether they have been invited, brief into the monthly quota they already have to hit, and replace paid amplification in your list of non-cash concessions with something that is worth actual money to them.
